facts.text: Baron was originally part of the Cherokee Nation lands within Indian Territory, with evidence of Native American habitation dating back centuries.
About one hundred Indian mounds on a hill south of Barren Fork Creek suggest the area was once inhabited by Caddo-like tribes.
Cherokee settlers established farms, sawmills, and grist mills along the local creek starting around 1828.
A severe drought in 1841 dried up the Illinois River, leading settlers to name the local tributary Barren Fork Creek.
Baron occupies the rolling foothills of the Ozark Plateau, featuring a landscape of deciduous woodlands and meandering drainages.
The community of Baron remains a quiet residential area with strong ties to its Cherokee heritage and local family cemeteries.
